statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-119379 is a heap buffer overflow in SQLite's session extension: when sqlite3changeset_apply() processes a changeset that repeats a table name in a later block with more columns, sessionUpdateFind() writes past its update-mask allocation. SQLite lists it as fixed in 3.54.0: https://sqlite.org/cves.html, https://sqlite.org/bugs/info/2026-08-16T10:15:25Z. The trunk fix is check-in https://sqlite.org/src/info/3f57024aecea0f3b, mirrored as https://github.com/sqlite/sqlite/commit/64459c87cc702d600704fb77ee40ca1782398a52, and the same change on the 3.53 maintenance branch is https://github.com/sqlite/sqlite/commit/ca7a4778bec356c3022dfa5d92ee67aaa17baa0c, which changes sessionChangesetApply() in ext/session/sqlite3session.c to detect the start of each table's block from the changeset iterator instead of comparing table names, and adds the sessioncorrupt.test regression test. DHI's 3.53.4-r1 build is SQLite 3.53.4 with a backport of the branch commit. The DHI Alpine 3.23 package repository publishes packages built from source sqlite (sqlite, sqlite-libs, sqlite-static, sqlite-dev and sqlite-doc) at 3.51.1-r0, 3.51.2-r0, 3.53.4-r0 and 3.53.4-r1, for x86_64 and aarch64. We unpacked the sqlite, sqlite-libs, sqlite-static and sqlite-dev packages of every one of those builds on both architectures, each checked against its index checksum. SQLite is compiled into three files in each build: the sqlite3 shell in the sqlite package, which carries its own copy and does not link libsqlite3; the shared library in sqlite-libs; and the static archive libsqlite3.a in sqlite-static. sqlite-dev holds only headers, a pkg-config file and the libsqlite3.so link. The shell and both libraries report SQLite 3.51.1, 3.51.2, 3.53.4 and 3.53.4 in those builds. The 3.51.1-r0, 3.51.2-r0 and 3.53.4-r0 builds are built from the upstream 3.51.1, 3.51.2 and 3.53.4 releases, none of which contains the fix. The session extension is compiled in: the compile-option list in the shell and both libraries of every build includes ENABLE_SESSION. We applied the 242-byte changeset from that regression test to a table t(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, v TEXT), with a test program linked once against the shared library and once against the static archive, for every build on x86_64 and aarch64 (the shell has no command that applies a changeset). In 3.51.1-r0, 3.51.2-r0 and 3.53.4-r0 the program crashes with a segmentation fault on both architectures, and on aarch64 valgrind reports invalid memory accesses; in 3.53.4-r1 sqlite3changeset_apply() returns SQLITE_OK on both architectures and valgrind on aarch64 reports no errors. The x86_64 runs used Docker Desktop's amd64 emulation. So 3.51.1-r0, 3.51.2-r0 and 3.53.4-r0 are affected and 3.53.4-r1 is fixed.
